function: Channel estimation of the downlink channel at each user and the uplink channel at the BS, with DnCNN denoisers trained by federated learning; ULNet reuses DLNet parameters (pp. 2-4).
system: Multi-user massive MIMO, hybrid architecture: BS 64 antennas and 16 RF chains, K=6 users with 4 antennas each, TDD, no RIS; frequency band not stated (pp. 2, 4).
method: DnCNN-based DLNet per user trained with FedSGD federated learning (supervised, labels from LS/MMSE estimates), then global parameters reused by ULNet at the BS (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Simulated channel realizations, M=1000 per user for training; the channel model is not specified and no standard model or measurement is named (p. 4).
test_conditions: Trained and tested in the same simulated setting; SNR sweep -2 to 5 dB, 600 samples per level; FL with 4 or 6 users; no unseen scenario (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Classical LS and LMMSE estimators; learned variants only: local DLNet, retrained ULNet, centralized learning (overhead only); no earlier published learned estimator compared (pp. 4-5).
metrics: NMSE versus SNR, test loss versus SNR, time complexity order versus channel size, communication overhead as number of transmitted symbols (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Fig. 5 plots the complexity order of DnCNN versus LS and LMMSE as a function of N_BS N_UE; no formula or parameter count given (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "we generate M = 1000 different channel realizations for each user"; the paper never names a channel model (no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measurement), so it is a custom simulation.
q2_support: p. 5: "We evaluate performance across different SNR levels, each with 600 samples"; no unseen scenario, band, array or user count is tested. The uplink reuse of the downlink parameters differs only in noise level (p. 3: "except for varying noise levels").
q3_support: p. 4: "the proposed approach outperforms the conventional LS/LMMSE estimators"; the learned comparisons are variants of the method (local DLNet, p. 4; retrained ULNet, p. 5: "comparable to those achieved by retraining"), and no earlier learned estimator such as [4]-[7] is compared.
q4_support: p. 5: "Fig. 5 illustrates the time complexity comparison between our proposed DnCNN-based FL and the other benchmark approaches"; the figure plots the complexity order against N_BS N_UE.
q5_support: p. 4: "we generate M = 1000 different channel realizations for each user"; channels are simulated with an unnamed model, and the paper gives no link to code or data and uses no public or measured dataset.
notes: Include, area 2: the learned channel estimator (DnCNN) is trained with digital federated learning (FedSGD gradients sent to the BS, not over the air), so it belongs to its function, not to area 7. q4=1 rests on the complexity-order plot of Fig. 5 (p. 5), with no formula written out; the FL overhead 2MNK on p. 5 is signaling and was not counted. q2=0 is borderline: the ULNet reuses the DLNet parameters (p. 4) but differs only in noise level (p. 3), which is an SNR change, and no other unseen condition is tested.
